source.workingTree: uncommitted isolated benchmark source; base HEAD alone does not identify this implementation

findings.mechanism: pre-admission or delayed not_found result invalidated a concurrent accepted operation
findings.repair: task-runtime.ts waitResult snapshots acceptance before the SDK query

findings.mechanism: unconfirmed tool cancellation became terminal error and allowed new model/tool effects
findings.repair: uncertain tool status atomically marks the attempt ambiguous

findings.mechanism: paused startup submitted after cleanup reported disposal
findings.repair: attempt lifetime guards, tracked pending operations, final SDK close and inactive wake/boot guards

findings.mechanism: stalled SDK abort/dispose blocked owned container destruction
findings.repair: independent bounded container stop; retain underlying coordinator close

findings.mechanism: stalled receipt persistence blocked owned container destruction
findings.repair: independent stop/fence/receipt observations with partial cleanup fields

findings.mechanism: process launch remained unobservably pending after caller abort
findings.repair: race launch with abort; kill/cancel a late arriving process best effort

findings.mechanism: output-limit error waited forever for stream cancellation acknowledgement
successful tool effect with lost receipt acknowledgement was rewritten as failure
findings.repair: separate execution and persistence failure; preserve unresolved effect and fence continuation

findings.mechanism: cleanup retry confirmed disposal while an earlier SDK close was still pending
findings.repair: single retained underlying close flight and final disposal after every earlier SDK call settles

checks.command: bun test bench/comparison/results.test.ts bench/comparison/runtime.test.ts bench/comparison/linux.test.ts bench/comparison/task.test.ts

assertionsInclude: task-probe SDK teardown disabled the physical Lifecycle alarm
parallel ordinary-task submissions admit exactly one attempt
cleanup retains the stopped receipt and tombstone

limits: This is a scoped code audit with simulated failure interleavings, not a production-readiness certificate.
Workerd smoke uses mocked provider HTTP/SSE and simulated tools; process/file integration runs on the macOS host.
Cancellation is signaled and late process stop is attempted; native descendant termination and provider cancellation remain unproved.
Native actor recreation, checkpoint/fault injection, provider interoperability/billing and snapshot quiescence remain unqualified.
Cleanup observers are bounded; underlying work can remain pending. Partial confirmation is not complete teardown.
The strict journal/uncertainty policy differs from upstream defaults and must remain disclosed in comparative measurements.
The diagnostic workload is not representative G0 qualification; no head-to-head task/cost/latency/security winner is established.
